title: Arthashastra
author: Kautilya (Chanakya)
blurb: India's ancient handbook of statecraft, by the strategist who helped build the Maurya empire: ministers, spies, money, punishment — and a king who must serve his people.

subjects.e: The king's subjects paid taxes in grain.

ministers.m: Senior advisers who help run a government.
ministers.e: The ministers met every morning with the king.

punishment.e: The punishment for littering is a fine.

contemptible.e: Cheating your own friends is contemptible.

cards.title: The king's happiness
cards.text: Kautilya's most famous line turns power upside down: a king's happiness lies in his people's happiness. He must not call good what pleases him, but what pleases them. So a king must always be active and alert.
cards.quote: In the happiness of his subjects lies his happiness; in their welfare his welfare
cards.qMean: A ruler is happy only when the people are happy.
cards.qLife: A school head who measures success by how the students are doing, not by her own awards.
cards.orig:
Of a king, the religious vow is his readiness to action; satisfactory discharge of duties is his performance of sacrifice; equal attention to all is the offer of fees and ablution towards consecration.

In the happiness of his subjects lies his happiness; in their welfare his welfare; whatever pleases himself he shall not consider as good, but whatever pleases his subjects he shall consider as good.

Hence the king shall ever be active and discharge his duties; the root of wealth is activity, and of evil its reverse.

cards.title: One wheel can't move
cards.text: Power can't be held alone. Just as a cart needs two wheels, a ruler needs ministers and their honest opinions.
cards.quote: A single wheel can never move.
cards.qMean: No one can rule or succeed alone.
cards.qLife: A startup founder who hires good people instead of doing everything herself.

Sovereignty (rdjatva) is possible only with assistance. A single wheel can never move. Hence he shall employ ministers and hear their opinion.

CHAPTER VIII. CREATION OF MINISTERS.

"THE King," says Bhdradvaja, "shall employ his classmates as his ministers; for they can be trusted by him inasmuch as he has personal knowledge of their honesty and capacity."

cards.title: Neither harsh nor soft
cards.text: Some teachers say rule by fear. Kautilya disagrees: too-harsh punishment makes a ruler hated, too-mild punishment makes him a joke. Only fair punishment, matched to the wrong, earns respect.
cards.quote: for whoever imposes severe punishment becomes repulsive to the people; while he who awards mild punishment becomes contemptible.
cards.qMean: Too much punishment makes people hate you; too little makes them not respect you.
cards.qLife: A parent whose rules are fair is obeyed more than one who shouts or one who never says no.
cards.orig:
"Hence," says my teacher, "whoever is desirous of the progress of the world shall ever hold the sceptre raised (udyatadanda). Never can there be a better instrument than the sceptre to bring people under control."

cards.title: Honey on the tongue
cards.text: Kautilya, a realist, says officials handling money will be tempted, as surely as you'd taste honey placed on your tongue. So a wise government doesn't rely on trust alone: it checks, rotates and audits its officers.
cards.quote: it is impossible not to taste the honey or the poison that finds itself at the tip of the tongue
cards.qMean: When you handle something tempting, it's almost impossible not to take a little.
cards.qLife: Why companies audit accounts even when they trust the accountant.
cards.orig:

cards.title: Fish in water
cards.text: Just as you can't see a fish drinking water, you can't easily see an official quietly taking money. Watch results and records, not appearances.
cards.quote: Just as fish moving under water cannot possibly be found out either as drinking or not drinking water, so government servants employed in the government work cannot be found out (while) taking money (for themselves).
cards.qMean: Hidden dishonesty is hard to spot, like a fish drinking underwater.
cards.qLife: Checking the stock count, not just the cashier's smile.
cards.orig:
… government servant not to eat up, at least, a bit of the king's revenue. Just as fish moving under water cannot possibly be found out either as drinking or not drinking water, so government servants employed in the government work cannot be found out (while) taking money (for themselves).

It is possible to mark the movements of birds flying high up in the sky; but not so is it possible to ascertain the movement of government servants of hidden purpose.

cards.title: Action is the king's prayer
cards.text: For a king, Kautilya says, the holy vow is being ready to act; doing his duties well is his sacrifice; treating everyone equally is his gift to the priests.
cards.quote: Of a king, the religious vow is his readiness to action
cards.qMean: A leader's true devotion is being ready to act.
cards.qLife: A manager who answers problems the same day instead of 'looking into it' for weeks.
